Highlights and needs attention

Progress recorded in the tracker, and items that are blocked, awaiting a decision, or near or past a target date. The Escalation Log has no entries.

Highlights

  • AY25.2.1 Comprehensive Training and Support Systems
    In Progress

    An initial inventory of university-wide trainings was completed, and an inventory document is in progress. A meeting with SDS, OIE, JHPS, and other partners was scheduled for April 20, 2026 to discuss JHPS policies and trainings.

  • AY25.2.2 Recommendation Tracking System
    In Progress

    The DIAC Recommendation Tracker was drafted. The tracker describes it as the initial implementation of this recommendation.

  • AY25.2.3 Appoint a DIAC Coordinator
    Partially Complete

    Dedicated DIAC coordination support is available at 0.5 FTE through the Advisor for Faculty and Staff Disability Inclusion role. The original recommendation called for 1.0 FTE.

  • AY24.1c Universal Design Guidelines for Construction
    In Progress

    HAWG is finalizing draft universal design guidelines for construction and renovation, following benchmarking and stakeholder engagement.

  • AY24.1a Recruitment and Retention of Employees with Disabilities
    Ongoing

    A presentation was made to UHRLT. The tracker notes it is awaiting next steps from HR partners.

  • AY24.2c Faculty Training on Inclusive Teaching Practices
    Complete and Ongoing

    The SDS Faculty Liaison program, new faculty module, open hours, and pro-rated tuition for Reduced Course Load were in place. These trainings were added to the larger training inventory.

Needs attention

  • AY24.3a MyChart Accessibility Improvements
    Blocked

    Discussed at the March 2026 DIAC meeting. Current governance does not support recommendations to JHHS at this time.

  • AY24.1b Central Accommodation Fund Establishment
    Planning

    A fund proposal has been drafted and is awaiting final estimates for the fund amount. The target date is TBD, and no owner is recorded.

  • AY24.3b Digital Accessibility Resource Expansion
    Ongoing

    The tracker notes the Director announced retirement and is leaving in July 2026. Position status is unknown.

  • AY25.2.1 Comprehensive Training and Support Systems
    In Progress

    Two implementation steps have FY26 targets, and FY26 ended June 30, 2026: AY25.2.1c (paused) and AY25.2.1d (not started).

AY25 recommendations | 3 total

AY25.1.1 Quick win

Leadership Visibility on Disability Inclusion

Not Started

Senior leaders should publicly affirm commitment to disability inclusion through regular communications that highlight the importance of access measures and accommodations, celebrate disability-related events, and support disability research.

Priority
●○○ Low
Progress
0%
Responsible party
Not recorded
Target
Q1 FY27
Latest update | Q1 FY27 | 04/02/26

DIAC continues to explore opportunities for leadership visibility on disability inclusion. Current institutional communications strategy is under review in light of external factors. DIAC will coordinate with University Communications and leadership to identify appropriate channels and timing.

Rationale, partners, and update history
Rationale

The 2023 Campus Climate Survey reveals significantly lower comfort and belonging among affiliates with disabilities. Apparent leadership support can improve campus climate and awareness of available resources.

Key implementation steps

Partner with University Communications, disability organizations, and affiliates conducting disability research to shape messaging and highlight community-driven improvements.

Key partners to engage

University Communications; Disability organizations (DiSCO, SGA Disability Caucus, Advocates for Disability Awareness, Equal Access for Science and Medicine, Access-ABLE); Disability Health Research Center; JHM Disability Employee Resource Group

Dependencies

Institutional communications strategy; External political/regulatory environment

Resource requirements

Minimal: coordination and approval only

Quarterly updates
  1. Q1 FY27 | 04/02/26
    DIAC continues to explore opportunities for leadership visibility on disability inclusion. Current institutional communications strategy is under review in light of external factors. DIAC will coordinate with University Communications and leadership to identify appropriate channels and timing.
AY25.1.2 Quick win

Streamline Communications Regarding Disability

Planning

Create clear communication channels between DIAC, divisions, and JHU disability and shared governance organizations. Streamline and clarify enterprise-wide communication that both highlights ongoing disability-related initiatives and communicates with disability cultural awareness.

Priority
●○○ Low
Progress
0%
Responsible party
Not recorded
Target
Q1 FY27
Latest update | Q1 FY27 | 04/02/26

DIAC is assessing current communication pathways and identifying opportunities to strengthen internal coordination. External-facing communications are being evaluated in context of broader institutional strategy. DIAC will advise on disability-aware communication practices as opportunities arise.

Rationale, partners, and update history
Rationale

Without established channels and points of contact, DIAC cannot gather community input, give feedback on university initiatives and policies, or share updates effectively.

Key implementation steps

Ensure community and key partners are aware of DIAC's recommendations and work in progress; ensure decision-makers consult with DIAC to gain and incorporate feedback before implementing projects.

Key partners to engage

University Communications; Divisions; Disability and shared governance organizations; Student Affairs; SDS; OIE

Dependencies

Institutional communications strategy; External political/regulatory environment

Resource requirements

Minimal: coordination and approvals only

Quarterly updates
  1. Q1 FY27 | 04/02/26
    DIAC is assessing current communication pathways and identifying opportunities to strengthen internal coordination. External-facing communications are being evaluated in context of broader institutional strategy. DIAC will advise on disability-aware communication practices as opportunities arise.

Universal Design Guidelines for Construction

Priority

Rationale, partners, and update history
Rationale

Accessibility is more than compliance. It is the intentional, universal design and adaptation of environments so that everyone can participate equitably.

The Hopkins Accessibility Working Group (HAWG) launched in Fall 2024; benchmarked accessibility efforts at other universities; engaged with stakeholders; consulted on projects; identified priorities outside of major projects; and began drafting guidelines for construction and renovations.

Questions for discussion

Questions from the August 10, 2026 working meeting for discussion with responsible stakeholders for each recommendation.

Implementation

Who owns implementation? Who is responsible for carrying it out?

Accountability

Who checks in to hold the responsible party accountable?

Outcomes

What are the desired outcomes, and how will success be measured? Should the department select its own outcomes and a realistic time frame?

Timeframe

Which goals are quick, medium-term, or longer-term?

Sharing updates

Where should DIAC updates and reports be posted (for example, the DIAC website), and is approval needed?

Appendix

Status definitions

Complete Deliverable finished and verified
Partially Complete A partial solution has been implemented or meaningful progress made; full implementation pending additional resources, decisions, or phased work
Ongoing Recurring or continuous activity with no fixed end date
In Progress Active implementation underway
Planning Scoping, identifying partners, or developing approach; no implementation yet
Not Started Work has not begun; no active planning underway
Blocked Work cannot proceed due to unresolved dependency, resource constraint, or need for escalation

Reporting cadence

Quarter Reporting period Update due
Q1 FY27 July to September 2026 October 1, 2026
Q2 FY27 October to December 2026 January 15, 2027
